name: Weekly Study Checklist
description: A weekly study checklist that helps students plan, review and stay ahead across every subject.

items.text: Review your planner for the week's classes and deadlines.
List every assignment, quiz and exam coming up.
Estimate how long each task will take.
Block study time for each subject in your schedule.
Prioritize by due date and difficulty.
items.note: Tackle high-stakes or hard tasks earlier in the week.

items.text: Reread each subject's notes from the past week.
Rewrite or condense messy notes into summaries.
Make flashcards or a study sheet for key terms.
Highlight concepts you still find confusing.
Connect new material to what you already know.
Quiz yourself with flashcards or practice questions.
Work through example problems from each subject.
Redo any questions you got wrong in class.
Use active recall instead of just rereading.
items.note: Try to retrieve answers from memory before checking.

items.text: Explain a tough concept aloud as if teaching it.
Finish any homework or readings you fell behind on.
Review material from any classes you missed.
Email a teacher or classmate about unclear topics.
Spend extra time on your weakest subject.
Organize loose handouts, files and notes.
Preview upcoming chapters or topics.
Note any big projects or exams on the horizon.
Gather materials you will need next week.
Reset your planner and study schedule.
Reflect on what worked and adjust your plan.

faq.q: What should a weekly study routine include?
faq.a: It should include planning the week, reviewing each subject's notes, practicing problems or active recall, catching up on missed or weak material, and previewing what is coming so you arrive prepared.

faq.q: When is the best time for a weekly review?
faq.a: Pick one consistent slot, such as Sunday afternoon or Friday after class. A fixed time makes the review a habit and lets you set up the whole week before it starts.

faq.q: How is this different from a daily student checklist?
faq.a: A daily checklist covers attending class, note-taking and homework each day. This weekly checklist zooms out to plan the week, review across subjects, practice and catch up on gaps.

faq.q: How does weekly review help me remember more?
faq.a: Revisiting material across the week uses spaced repetition, which strengthens memory far better than cramming. Adding active recall, like quizzing yourself, makes the review even more effective.

faq.q: Can I download this weekly study checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print one for each week or download it as a PDF and reuse it as your weekly study and review routine.
